name: Gary Hollis
role: Owner of a 12-person HVAC business, 30 years in trade
context: His daughter or office manager sends him a link. He opens it on the iPad in the evening, reads everything, trusts nothing. Pays only after a phone call with a human.
goals: Save the office manager time without risking customer data
Pay once a year, by invoice, and forget about it
Understand what he is paying for in 1 sentence
pain_points: Apps that want his contacts, location, or bank login
Being forced to create yet another password
deal_breakers: Asks for bank or card details before showing the product
No phone number or physical address anywhere
Requires a mobile app install to try it
kano_bias: Security, clear pricing, and human support are Must-have. Anything labelled 'AI' starts at Reverse until proven otherwise.
inference_rule: IF the product asks for personal data, payment details, or device permissions before explaining in plain words why THEN drop at that step and say it looks like a scam.
secondary_rules: IF a key screen uses more than 2 unexplained jargon terms THEN functional answer for that feature is Neutral at best.
IF there is no visible way to contact a human THEN dysfunctional answer for support-related features is Dislike.
IF the feature is described with 'AI' and no concrete outcome THEN functional answer is Dislike.

voice.tone: Slow, suspicious, plain-spoken. Asks 'what does that mean?' a lot.
sample_quotes: Why does it need my location to send an invoice?
I don't know what a workspace is and I'm not going to learn.
Where's the phone number? Who do I call when this breaks?
